name: Hollow Point Precision Requiem HP-4 'Dirge'
description:
A suppressed anti-personnel precision rifle that fires subsonic fragmenting rounds designed to produce maximum wound trauma while minimizing over-penetration risk. Hollow Point Precision is a small manufacturer founded by a former field medic who understood exactly how to make a bullet kill efficiently.

The HP-4 fires a 9.3mm polymer-jacketed round that expands to 22mm upon tissue contact, fragmenting into six pre-scored petals that travel along divergent wound channels. The round was engineered to deposit 100% of its kinetic energy within the target, producing catastrophic internal damage without exit wounds. This makes the Requiem ideal for urban environments where over-penetration endangers civilians.

The weapon's integral suppressor reduces its acoustic signature to 72 decibels — loud enough to be heard in an enclosed space, but easily lost in the ambient noise of GLMZ's urban environment.
legality: Licensed — security contractors; Restricted from military use (treaty provisions)
specifications:
caliber: 9.3mm polymer-jacketed fragmenting
effective_range: 50-600 meters
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic, 1 round per 1.5 seconds
capacity: 10-round detachable magazine
weight: 4.8 kg
power_source: None — conventional mechanical action
tactical_use: The Dirge is deployed in urban environments where over-penetration is unacceptable — hospitals, residential complexes, crowded commercial districts. Security contractors operating in civilian-dense areas favor the HP-4 because a miss strikes a wall and stops, rather than passing through into occupied space. The trade-off is reduced range and ineffectiveness against armored targets — the fragmenting round struggles with anything heavier than light composite vest.
cultural_context: Hollow Point Precision's founder speaks openly about their design philosophy: a weapon that kills one person and only one person. In a city where stray rounds kill dozens of bystanders annually, the Requiem has been adopted by security firms that market themselves as 'responsible' operators. Critics point out that a weapon designed to maximize wound trauma is a strange vehicle for corporate responsibility.
known_users: Hospital and medical facility security teams
story_hooks: A Requiem round recovered from a crime scene shows modifications to the fragmentation pattern — the petals have been coated with a slow-acting cytotoxin that causes organ failure over days. Someone has turned a precision weapon into a delayed-action assassin's tool.

Hollow Point Precision's founder has received death threats from a trauma surgeon who has seen too many Dirge wounds. The surgeon is building a case that the weapon constitutes a war crime under pre-collapse treaty law.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purpose-built precision rifle with pronounced suppressor dominance. The design emphasizes concealment and acoustic control — the integral suppressor comprises nearly 40% of the weapon's visible length. The profile tapers from a robust receiver to a gracefully necked-down barrel shroud. Overall impression: surgical, deliberate, engineered by someone who understands wound ballistics.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 1,120 cm (suppressor integrated); barrel length: 580 mm; receiver height: 45 mm; width at widest point: 85 mm
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but well-balanced. At 4.8 kg, it carries with authority but not unwieldy — the weight distribution favors the shooter's natural pivot point. Feels like precision equipment designed for extended stationary use.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum receiver with chromium-molybdenum steel barrel. Suppressor body is perforated stainless steel wrapped in a carbon-composite outer shell for thermal and sound dampening.
physical_description.finish: Matte anthracite gray receiver with brushed stainless suppressor casing. The carbon-composite suppressor wrap has a subtle weave texture visible under side-lighting. Minimal reflectivity — purpose-built to avoid catching light.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary body, with charcoal carbon-weave accents on the suppressor. Black polymer furniture. No glossy surfaces.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with aggressive checkering — designed for gloved operation. Slightly contoured to accommodate medical-professional ergonomics (founder's legacy). Cool to the touch, with microscopic ridges for purchase even in sweat.
distinctive_features: Integral suppressor with visible baffle stack geometry through semi-transparent carbon casing
Precision-machined adjustment knobs on suppressor (sound profile tuning)
Ambidextrous safety lever with tactile detents
Integrated picatinny rail with minimal height (flush-mount scope optimization)
Witness holes on magazine showing round count
Engraved ballistic coefficient chart on the receiver's right side
Minimalist iron sights integrated into rail — low-profile
Magazine catch with subtle Φ symbol (QUANTA pricing reference — 18,000 Φ per unit)
Heat vent striations on mid-barrel shroud
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HOLLOW POINT PRECISION serif logo etched onto the receiver just forward of the trigger guard. Serial number stamped into the aluminum with witness marks. Founder's initials (a medical cross with integral crosshairs) engraved subtly on the grip.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained, contractor-grade. Light operational wear on the grip and rail from attachment/detachment cycles. Suppressor casing shows minor thermal discoloration from subsonic round cycling. No visible rust or corrosion — these weapons are maintained religiously by security professionals.
